title: Anna & Milo
description: Anna and Milo have been an inseparable couple for several years. A well-regarded literature teacher, Milo is calm and predictable. But for the past six months, his behavior has become opaque: secret calls

questions.question: Milo has been getting calls these past few days from someone suspicious... Can you tell me who comes up the most?
questions.hint: Open the Phone app and look in the Recent tab. Look for who appears most often in recent calls, especially last night.

questions.question: Anouk... that's weird, this name keeps coming up... What's her job?
questions.hint: Go to Contacts and look for Anouk Desmet's contact info to see her profession.

questions.question: A literary agent? But Milo doesn't write, he's a teacher... Do they see each other often? Tell me how many times they've met in the past 30 days please
questions.hint: Open the Calendar app in monthly view and count all events titled 'RDV A.' over the past 30 days.

questions.question: 6 times already with this chick... He's seeing her during our relationship... Has he ever sent her money, if so, tell me how much?
questions.hint: Open the Revolut app, go to transaction history and filter by 'Desmet'. Look for a recent transfer.

questions.question: 1,200€? That much! Give me the name on the account he sent it to, I'm going to dispute it...
questions.hint: In Revolut, find the 1,200€ transfer to Cabinet Desmet and look at the transaction details to see the company name on the account.

questions.question: A publishing house...? What exactly is he doing with them, tell me what he wrote?
questions.hint: Open Gmail and search for an email from Éditions Soleil from 3 weeks ago with acceptance of something as the subject.

questions.question: A manuscript... so that means he's secretly writing a novel? Who else knew about it?
questions.hint: In WhatsApp, some messages are protected by a code. The hint mentions 'the average of the best class'. First go to Pronote to find which class has the best average, then use this info as the code in WhatsApp. Then look for a conversation with someone congratulating Milo.

questions.question: How long has he been working on this manuscript?
questions.hint: Go further back in the WhatsApp conversation with Théo to find out how long he's been covering for Milo regularly.

questions.question: 1 year that Théo has been lying to me too... What exactly did he write in this novel... Tell me who the main character of the story is.
questions.hint: In the Notes app, look for a locked note titled 'Manuscript'. To find the code, go to the Calendar and look for an annual event with hearts and their 2 names. The date of this event will be the code to unlock the note.

questions.question: The novel is inspired by me… it's so touching, so sweet. What's it going to be called?
questions.hint: Go to Safari, there's already a page open on Amazon KDP where you'll see the pre-order for Milo's book with its title.

questions.question: And when is this book being published? Does it have a release date?
questions.hint: Go back to Gmail and find the email from Éditions Soleil with 'contract' in the subject. Open the PDF attachment and look for the line 'Expected publication date'.

questions.question: September 13, 2026… but that's our relationship anniversary! He's preparing something special for that day, I'm so excited, tell me what it is!
questions.hint: Go to the Drive app, 'Personal' folder, and find a locked PDF. The code is Milo and Anna's relationship anniversary date. The file contains an aerodrome address. Then, go to Instagram and search for that aerodrome's account to understand what happens there at 6 AM.

textSuccess: Oh my god... Milo... All this time, you were writing a novel about us? And that hot air balloon for our anniversary... I was so stupid to doubt you. I'm going to go see you right now and apologize. You're the most romantic man in the world and I went through your phone like an idiot. Thank you for helping me understand... I can't wait to read this book!

onboardingContent.text: Hey... My name is Anna and I really need your help. A friend told me you were good at solving mysteries. It's urgent.
I've been with Milo for three years. We were inseparable, we talked about marriage, kids... I thought I knew everything about him.
But for the past six months, he's become secretive. Secret calls, mysterious meetings, strange transfers... He's lying to me and it's eating me up inside.
I managed to get access to his phone while he's sleeping. Help me find out what he's hiding from me. I'm counting on you.

# PUBLISHING CONTRACT

> **ÉDITIONS SOLEIL**  
> *Simplified joint-stock company with capital of €150,000*  
> *RCS Paris 834 592 110 — SIRET 834 592 110 00018*  
> *12 rue des Éditeurs, 75011 Paris*

---

**BETWEEN THE UNDERSIGNED**

**On one hand**, the company **Éditions Soleil**, SAS with capital of one hundred fifty thousand (150,000) euros, registered in the Trade and Companies Register of Paris under number 834 592 110, whose registered office is located at 12 rue des Éditeurs, 75011 Paris, represented by Ms. **Camille Marchand**, acting in her capacity as general manager, duly authorized for the purposes hereof,  
hereinafter referred to as "**the Publisher**";

**On the other hand**, Mr. **Milo Weber**, born November 27, 1996 in Berlin (Germany), of German nationality, residing at 14 Akazienweg, 10317 Berlin (Federal Republic of Germany), tax number: DE-284 731 905,  
hereinafter referred to as "**the Author**";

The Publisher and the Author being hereinafter referred to individually as a "**Party**" and collectively as the "**Parties**".

**THE FOLLOWING HAS BEEN PREVIOUSLY STATED:**

The Author has submitted to the Publisher an original novel manuscript provisionally titled **"Les Voix du Silence"**, which was favorably evaluated by the Publisher's reading committee on June 30, 2026. The Parties wish to formalize the conditions for editing and marketing this work.

**THIS BEING STATED, THE FOLLOWING HAS BEEN AGREED AND DECIDED:**

---

## ARTICLE 1 — SUBJECT OF THE CONTRACT

**1.1.** The purpose of this contract is the assignment by the Author to the Publisher of the editing, reproduction, distribution and marketing rights of the novel manuscript submitted under the working title **"Les Voix du Silence"** (hereinafter the "**Work**"), as part of the *Contemporary Literature* collection of Éditions Soleil.

**1.2.** The final title of the Work will be agreed upon by mutual agreement between the Parties no later than thirty (30) days before the manufacturing date. In the absence of agreement, the working title will be retained.

## ARTICLE 2 — MANUSCRIPT DELIVERY AND AUTHOR OBLIGATIONS

**2.1.** The Author undertakes to deliver to the Publisher the final manuscript of the Work, in digital version in .docx or .odt format, no later than **July 27, 2026**. The manuscript must be complete, proofread by the Author and comply with the typographic standards provided by the Publisher.

**2.2.** The Author guarantees that the Work is original, that it does not in any way constitute counterfeiting or plagiarism, that it does not infringe the rights of third parties, and that it has not been subject to any prior assignment incompatible with these presents.

**2.3.** In case of delivery delay exceeding thirty (30) days, the Publisher may, after formal notice that remains ineffective for fifteen (15) days, terminate this contract by right, without compensation and without prejudice to the restitution of sums possibly paid as advance.

## ARTICLE 3 — PROOFREADING

**3.1.** The Publisher will send the Author proofs of the Work for proofreading and correction. The Author will have a period of **fifteen (15) working days** from receipt to return the corrected proofs.

**3.2.** After this period without return, the print approval (BAT) will be deemed tacitly acquired. Author corrections exceeding ten percent (10%) of the initial composition volume will be billed to the Author at the actual recomposition cost.

**3.3.** The Publisher reserves the right to make minor spelling, grammatical and typographical corrections without prior approval from the Author, provided that the meaning of the text is not altered.

## ARTICLE 4 — PUBLICATION SCHEDULE

**Expected publication date:** **September 13, 2026**, in paper (paperback) and digital (ePub, Kindle) formats, subject to proper completion of manufacturing, indexing with distributors (Hachette Distribution, Dilicom) and logistics delivery.

The Publisher undertakes to put the Work on sale within a maximum period of **eighteen (18) months** from delivery of the compliant final manuscript. After this period, the Author may request termination of the contract under the conditions provided in article 11.

## ARTICLE 5 — PRINTING, REPRINTING AND PULPING

**5.1.** The first print run is set at **three thousand (3,000) copies** in paperback format. The Publisher may proceed with a complementary print run of a maximum of five hundred (500) copies without amendment, within the limits of the printer's capacity.

**5.2.** Any reprint beyond 3,500 cumulative copies will be subject to prior notification to the Author, accompanied by the number of copies envisaged. The Author will have ten (10) days to make observations.

**5.3.** The Publisher may proceed with pulping unsold copies after a minimum period of twenty-four (24) months following the date of sale, subject to informing the Author in writing thirty (30) days in advance. The Author will have the option to buy back all or part of the copies destined for pulping at cost price excluding rights.

## ARTICLE 6 — SELLING PRICE

The public selling price of the Work will be freely set by the Publisher in accordance with law no. 81-766 of October 22, 1981 relating to book prices. As an indication, the public selling price envisaged at the signing date is **nineteen euros and ninety cents (€19.90)** including VAT for the paperback format and **nine euros and ninety-nine cents (€9.99)** including VAT for the digital format.

## ARTICLE 7 — ASSIGNED RIGHTS AND TERRITORY

**7.1.** The Author assigns to the Publisher, on an exclusive basis, for the whole world and for the entire duration of protection of the Work by copyright as provided by the Intellectual Property Code, the following rights:

- right of reproduction on any material medium known or unknown to date;
- right of representation by any process;
- right of translation into all languages;
- right of adaptation, including in audio format (audiobook).

**7.2.** The Author retains his moral right over the Work, in accordance with articles L. 121-1 et seq. of the Intellectual Property Code. Any substantial modification of the text must receive the prior written agreement of the Author.

## ARTICLE 8 — AUTHOR REMUNERATION

**8.1. Proportional rights.** The Author will receive proportional remuneration of **eight percent (8%)** calculated on the public selling price excluding taxes of each copy sold, all editions and formats combined, after deduction of returns, press copies (50 maximum) and author copies (20 free copies).

**8.2. Advance.** The Publisher will pay the Author, upon signing this contract, a non-refundable advance of **one thousand two hundred euros (€1,200)**, chargeable against future proportional rights. This advance will be paid by bank transfer within fifteen (15) days following receipt of the contract signed by both Parties.

**8.3. Account rendering.** The Publisher will send the Author, no later than the last day of the civil quarter following the period considered, a detailed statement of sales, returns, stocks and acquired rights. Payment of rights exceeding the advance will occur within thirty (30) days following sending of the statement.

**8.4. Right of verification.** The Author may, once a year and at his expense, have the Publisher's accounts verified by a certified public accountant of his choice, subject to thirty (30) days' notice.

## ARTICLE 9 — DERIVATIVE RIGHTS

**9.1.** The assignment includes the following derivative rights: pocket edition, club edition, enhanced digital edition, audiobook, translation, and audiovisual exploitation (film, television, series or podcast adaptation).

**9.2.** Net revenue received by the Publisher from exploitation of derivative rights will be shared equally (**50% / 50%**) between the Publisher and the Author, after deduction of assignment fees and possible agent commissions.

**9.3.** The Publisher undertakes to inform the Author of any offer to acquire derivative rights within fifteen (15) days following its receipt, and not to conclude any audiovisual adaptation agreement without the prior written consent of the Author.

## ARTICLE 10 — RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL

**10.1.** The Author grants the Publisher a right of first refusal on his **next two (2) works** of the same literary genre (novel, literary fiction).

**10.2.** The Author undertakes to submit the manuscript of each work covered by this right of first refusal to the Publisher as a priority. The Publisher will have **three (3) months** from receipt of the complete manuscript to notify its decision. In the absence of response within this period, the Author will recover full freedom for the work concerned.

## ARTICLE 11 — TERMINATION

**11.1.** In case of serious breach by one of the Parties of its obligations under this contract, the other Party may pronounce termination by right thirty (30) days after sending a formal notice that remains ineffective, sent by registered mail with acknowledgment of receipt.

**11.2.** The following notably constitute serious breach: failure to publish within the period provided in article 4, non-payment of author rights for two consecutive quarters, or exhaustion of the Work without reprinting for a continuous period of eighteen (18) months despite a written request from the Author.

**11.3.** In case of termination, the assigned rights will return to the Author by right, subject to the disposal of existing stock for a period of six (6) months. The Publisher must send the Author a final account statement within sixty (60) days following termination.

## ARTICLE 12 — GENERAL PROVISIONS

**12.1.** This contract is subject to French law, and notably to the provisions of articles L. 131-1 et seq. of the Intellectual Property Code.

**12.2.** Any dispute relating to the validity, interpretation or execution of this contract will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of **Paris**, after attempting amicable resolution for a minimum duration of sixty (60) days.

**12.3.** This contract constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and cancels and replaces any prior agreement, correspondence or commitment relating to its subject.

**12.4.** Personal data necessary for the execution of this contract will be processed in accordance with regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR). Each Party undertakes to process the other Party's data only to the extent strictly necessary for the execution of its contractual obligations.

messages.content: I need a creative writing exercise on magical realism for my literature students. Do you have any simple and effective ideas?

Perfect! Here are 4 simple and effective proposals for a magical realism exercise in literature class:

- The object that comes to life: a notebook forgotten in the courtyard tells what the characters don't say.
- The broken temporal passage: a scene where present and past respond to each other without transition.
- The dialogue without subject: two objects start talking as if they had a private life.
- The open ending: leave a question unanswered to encourage class discussion.

Implementation tips:
- limit to 15-20 lines per text
- ask for 3 point of view choices
- vary the register according to the students' level.

Would you like me to prepare a mini-exercise booklet ready to print?
Can you suggest a literary itinerary in Berlin for my classes and free time?

Of course! Here's a literary itinerary in Berlin that combines literary venues, bookstores and cafés perfect for writing:

- Literaturhaus Berlin (Fasanenstraße) — iconic venue for meetings, readings and exhibitions.
- Dussmann das KulturKaufhaus (Friedrichstraße) — huge bookstore with comfortable reading spaces.
- Café Einstein Stammhaus (Kurfürstenstraße) — historic café popular with writers.
- Berliner Ensemble — theater and contemporary texts, stimulating atmosphere.
- Sankt Oberholz (Rosenthaler Platz) — café frequented by young writers and freelancers, great atmosphere for writing.

Would you like me to map out a route for half a day or a full day?
What recent German works would you recommend for my students?

For literature students, here are 3 recent German novels that work well in class, with why they work:

- Herkunft — Saša Stanišić (2019): themes of identity and migration; clear style and lively dialogue; quite accessible.
- Unterleuten — Juli Zeh (2016): choral novel about a village; precise language and social connections; excellent for discussing community dynamics.
- Altes Land — Dörte Hansen (2020): family novel; modern language and intergenerational memory; beautiful window into the German rural landscape.

If you'd like, I can add reading guides and questions for each work.

messages.content: How to prepare a workshop on voice work and dialogue in class?

Here's a proposal for a 90-minute workshop:

Objectives: develop intonation, rhythm, active listening and voice work for dialogue.
Materials: short excerpts (2–3 pages) from a novel, dialogue sheets, audio recorder, feedback notebook.
Structure:
1) Silent reading in pairs (5 min)
2) Expressive reading in pairs (7 min)
3) Dialogue work: rewrite an exchange by modifying the tone and emotions (15 min)
4) Staging: 2-minute mini-scene in front of the group (10–12 min)
5) Feedback and self-assessment (10 min)

Assessment: vocal presence, clarity of intentions and cooperation.
Resources: selection of excerpts and performance criteria checklist.
Help with writing an article on the importance of literary translation.

Article outline:

Title: Why literary translation is essential for cross-cultural exchange

Introduction: how translation opens worlds and crosses boundaries.

Sections:
- Fidelity vs interpretation: when translating, what can change and why?
- Cultural transmission: word choices that convey values and imagery.
- The translator as author: the writing behind translation and stylistic choices.
- Concrete examples: famous passages and translation variants.
- Ethical and linguistic issues: respecting originals and audiences.

Conclusion: call to value translators' work and encourage language learning.

Format ideas: blog post series, educational resource, and writing workshop around translated passages.
How to integrate music and poetry in a literature class?

Here's a planned workshop outline:

Objectives: perceive rhythm, tone and meaning in poems, then write a piece as a musical response.
MATERIALS: a selection of short poems, a suitable playlist, paper and headphones, audio editing software (optional).
Process:
1) Guided listening to a poem set to music and discussion about feelings (10 min)
2) Quick analysis of rhythm and imagery (10 min)
3) Writing workshop: write a quatrain or rondeau inspired by the piece (20 min)
4) Voice work and performance (15 min)
5) Discussion and feedback (10 min)

Resources: lists of poems in audio version and recommended playlists.

Tip: adapt the choice of pieces to the students' level and the course's focus.
I'd like to write a novel about the Berlin life of a young literature teacher; do you have any ideas?

Here are 6 ideas for a novel about the Berlin life of a young teacher:

- Daily life in a Berlin school: between disciplinary meetings and passion for literature, the protagonist keeps a narrative journal and shares excerpts with Anna Fischer, his girlfriend.
- Writing as connection: Anouk Desmet, literary agent, pushes the protagonist to write more intense texts to attract the right collaboration.
- The neighborhood as character: Kreuzberg and Mitte influence the stories, the cafés and markets that, day by day, discover the readers.
- The tension between tradition and modernity: the novel's tool is dialogue and the passage of time, calls and messages that pace the chapters.
- A secret workshop: a week of writing outside school where Milo's students and friends cross paths.
- Romance and friendship: weaving Anna Fischer and Théo Müller into meaningful scenes, not forgetting Stef Schmidt as witness to the choices.

If you want, I can turn these ideas into more detailed synopses for a chapter-by-chapter outline.
What digital resources and tools for teaching literature?

Here are some useful digital resources and tools for teaching literature:

- Collaboration tools: Google Docs, Notion, Trello — for co-writing documents and planning lessons.
- Reference management: Zotero, JabRef, BibTeX — for organizing sources and references.
- Course platforms: Moodle, Canvas — for structuring assignments and assessments.
- Writing and AI tools (to be used with critical thinking): writing assistants, prompt generators, revision assistants — use them to stimulate creativity while teaching critical thinking.
- Open digital resources: Project Gutenberg-DE, Zeno.org and other open libraries for classic German texts.
- Layout and presentation tools: Canva, Google Slides, Adobe Spark — for creating attractive visual materials.
- Podcasts and videos: university libraries, YouTube EDU and literary podcasts for text analysis.

Tip: create resource packs by theme (poetry, novel, theater) and share them with students via your LMS.

files.content:
# Synopsis table – novel in progress

Characters: Milo, Anna, Théo, Stef, and some secondary characters.

Plot: The teacher travels through time through metaphorical description and encounters a network of writers living in Berlin.

Themes: power of words, trust, artistic creation, obstacles.

Novel's objective: demonstrate how a community of teachers can change a city by exploring arts and literature.

Plan: 4 acts, 12 chapters, 2 scenes before and 2 scenes after each chapter.

Course date: July 19, 2026

Theme: 19th century German literature – Göttingen and Berlin.

Key points:
- The bildungsroman and concepts of realism and idealization.
- Analysis of figures like Büchner, Fontane and Eichendorff.
- Teaching techniques: plan guided writing periods and contextual quotations.

- Passage examination, small group discussion, writing a short essay
- Exercises on literary vocabulary and imagery.

Assessment: attendance, participation and a 900-word mini-essay.

Notes: the text is inspired by 20th-century German poets and my own experiences at the University of Berlin.

files.name: Novel_plan.md
files.content:
# Novel Plan – Berlin 1920

Objective: write a historical novel that explores the intellectual and social tensions of Berlin after the war.

## Main Characters
- Milo Weber (literature teacher, narrator)
- Anna Fischer (girlfriend, potential editor)
- Théo Müller (close friend, journalist)
- Stef Schmidt (close friend, librarian)

## Main Plot
1. The protagonist prepares a course on Brecht and theater
2. A secret meeting is organized at dawn near Tempelhof airport
3. A found letter endangers the characters' living situation

## Time Frame
- Year: 1920
- Locations: Berlin-Mitte, Kreuzberg, temporary airport near the city

## Structure
- Part 1: Introduction of characters and setting
- Part 2: Unfolding of events and revelation
- Part 3: Resolution and questioning about the meaning of writing

## Research and References
- Oral histories of rural teachers in Germany
- Studies on theater of the period and the role of intellectuals

# Private Journal

Today I prepared my German literature courses for the Berlin students, focusing on how to present works in their original language. I rewrote some notes to make them clearer for beginners.

On July 24, 2026, I met Anna Fischer to discuss organizing a literary trip in November.

I had to remind myself of my priorities: grading time, personal writing time, and moments with my friends Anna and Théo.

Tomorrow, I'm going to read the poetry collection by Rainer Maria Rilke and prepare a short presentation for the student group.

The coming weeks will be intense but stimulating.
